lessons.title: Where is Cameroon? Regions and regional capitals

lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)

objectives: Say where Cameroon is and name its neighbours.
Name the ten regions of Cameroon and their capitals.
Name the capital city and the two official languages.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; dates and names to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
Area (about 475,000 km²) and regional capitals are standard facts; check against the textbook. 'Africa in miniature' is a common nickname.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Location
blocks.md: Cameroon is in **Central Africa**, just north of the **Equator**. It has a coast on the **Atlantic Ocean** (the Gulf of Guinea). Its neighbours are **Nigeria** (west), **Chad** (north-east), the **Central African Republic** (east), the **Republic of the Congo**, **Gabon** and **Equatorial Guinea** (south). The area is about 475,000 square kilometres.

blocks.title: Capital and languages
blocks.md: The political capital is **Yaoundé**. **Douala** is the biggest city and the main port. The two official languages are **English** and **French**, and there are also many national languages. Cameroon is often called **Africa in miniature** because it has forests, mountains, savanna, a coast and a desert edge.

blocks.caption: The ten regions of Cameroon and their capitals.
blocks.alt: Ten boxes. Each shows a region and its capital: Adamawa, Ngaoundéré; Centre, Yaoundé; East, Bertoua; Far North, Maroua; Littoral, Douala; North, Garoua; North-West, Bamenda; West, Bafoussam; South, Ebolowa; South-West, Buea.

blocks.title: Remembering the regions
blocks.md: There are **10 regions**. Three are in the **north** (Far North, North, Adamawa). Two are **English-speaking** regions in the west (North-West and South-West). The others are Centre, East, Littoral, South and West. Learn them with the capitals in pairs: Littoral-Douala, West-Bafoussam, South-West-Buea.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Mixing up the **capital of Cameroon** (Yaoundé) and the **biggest city** (Douala).
- Confusing a region with its capital (the Littoral is the region; Douala is its capital).
- Writing *North West* and *Northwest* in different ways: use *North-West* and *South-West*.
- Saying that Cameroon is in West Africa only.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Give the capital of the South-West Region and the capital of the Far North Region.
steps: South-West: the regional capital is Buea.
Far North: the regional capital is Maroua.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name three neighbours of Cameroon and say in which direction each one lies.
steps: Chad is to the north-east, and Gabon is to the south.

objectives: Describe the main relief regions: coastal plain, plateaus, highlands, northern plains.
Name Mount Cameroon, the main rivers and two lakes.
Say why rivers and mountains are useful.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; dates and names to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
Height of Mount Cameroon is given as 'about 4,000 m' because books give slightly different figures (e.g. 4,040 m).
Relief profile is schematic, not a real map.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Relief
blocks.md: **Relief** means the shape of the land. Cameroon has: the low **coastal plain** on the Atlantic; the **Southern plateau** (the forest zone); the **Western highlands** (the Grassfields, with high hills and volcanic mountains); the **Adamawa plateau** in the centre; and the flat **northern plains** towards Lake Chad and the River Benue.

blocks.caption: A simple profile of the land from the coast to the north.
blocks.alt: A green hill-shaped profile. The land is low at the coast, rises to a highest peak near Mount Cameroon, falls over plateaus and highlands, and is low again in the northern plains.

blocks.title: Mount Cameroon
blocks.md: **Mount Cameroon** (also called **Fako**) is the highest mountain in Cameroon, about 4,000 metres high. It is an **active volcano** near Buea and Limbe, in the South-West Region. People climb it for sport, and farmers use the fertile volcanic soil around it.

blocks.title: Rivers and lakes
blocks.md: Important rivers: the **Sanaga** (the longest river wholly in Cameroon), the **Wouri** (flows into the sea near Douala), the **Benue** (flows north-west to Nigeria) and the **Logone** (flows toward Lake Chad). **Lake Chad** is in the far north and is shared with other countries. **Lake Nyos** is a small crater lake in the North-West. Rivers give water, fish, transport and **hydroelectric power**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that Mount Cameroon is in the North or in the West: it is in the **South-West**.
- Thinking that all rivers flow to the same sea: some flow to the Atlantic, some to the Niger and some to Lake Chad.
- Mixing up **relief** (shape of the land) with **climate** (weather).

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: In which region is Mount Cameroon, and what kind of mountain is it?
steps: Mount Cameroon stands near Buea and Limbe.
Buea and Limbe are in the South-West Region, and the mountain is an active volcano.
blocks.answer: In the South-West Region; it is an active volcano.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Give two uses of a river such as the Sanaga.
steps: People use river water for farming and fishing.
Dams on the Sanaga produce electricity, and rivers can also carry boats.
blocks.answer: Fishing and electricity (also water for farming, transport).

objectives: Describe the two main climates of Cameroon and the seasons.
Name the vegetation zones and some plants and animals of each.
Explain why the north is drier than the south.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; dates and names to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
Exact months of the seasons vary by region and year: given loosely. Reserves named (Korup, Dja, Waza) are well known; wildlife examples simplified.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Climate
blocks.md: **Climate** is the usual weather of a place over many years. The **south** of Cameroon has a **hot, wet equatorial climate** with **two rainy seasons and two dry seasons**. The **north** is **hotter and drier** with **one rainy season** (about May to October) and a long dry season. The **highlands** are cooler. Weather also changes with height: it is cooler on mountains.

items.text: North: Sahel and savanna, one rainy season

blocks.caption: Rainfall gets less from the south to the north.
blocks.alt: Three bands. The northern band says Sahel and savanna with one rainy season. The middle band says savanna and highlands. The southern band says rainforest with two rainy seasons. An arrow points to the south for wetter.

blocks.title: Vegetation zones
blocks.md:
- **Equatorial rainforest** (south and east): tall trees, thick leaves, many animals (monkeys, elephants, gorillas in reserves). Korup and Dja are forest reserves.
- **Savanna** (centre, Adamawa, Grassfields): grass with scattered trees.
- **Sahel / dry savanna** (far north): short grass, thorny trees; Waza National Park protects lions and elephants.
- **Mangroves** grow along the coast.

blocks.title: Harmattan
blocks.md: In the dry season a dry, dusty wind called the **Harmattan** blows from the Sahara. It makes the air dusty and cool at night, and lips and skin dry. Wearing warm clothes at night and drinking water helps. People in the north feel it most.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that the whole country has the same climate.
- Thinking that rainforest means it is raining all day: it has dry months too.
- Mixing **weather** (today) and **climate** (over many years).
- Forgetting that the highlands (West, North-West) are cooler than the lowlands.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Why does the south grow cocoa and the north grow cotton?
steps: Cocoa needs a lot of rain and heat: the south is wet.
Cotton needs a long sunny dry season: the north has one rainy season and a long dry one.
blocks.answer: Cocoa likes the wet, warm south; cotton likes the drier north.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name two differences between the climate of Douala and of Maroua.
steps: Douala is on the coast: hot, very wet, with two rainy seasons.
Maroua is in the far north: hot, much drier, with one short rainy season.
blocks.answer: Douala is wetter with two rainy seasons; Maroua is drier with one.

lessons.title: Economic activities and transport

objectives: Name the main economic activities and the regions where they are important.
Tell primary, secondary and tertiary activities apart.
Name the main means of transport and a few ports, railways and airports.
reviewNotes: Facts about Cameroon are limited to well-established, neutral points; dates and names to be checked by a teacher against the official textbook.
Regions named for each crop are simplified (several crops grow in several regions). Port of Kribi and railway lines are well known but their details (dates, capacity) are not given.
Petroleum is mentioned in general terms only; no production figures.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Economic activities
blocks.md: People work to earn money and to produce what we need. **Primary** activities take things from nature: farming, fishing, herding, forestry and mining. **Secondary** activities change them into other goods: factories, food processing, sawmills. **Tertiary** activities are services: trade, transport, banks, teaching, health care and tourism.

blocks.caption: Primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: primary (farming, fishing, mining), secondary (factories, processing) and tertiary (trade, transport, schools).

blocks.title: Farming and other activities
blocks.md:
- **Cash crops**: cocoa (Centre, South, South-West), coffee (West, South-West, Littoral), cotton (North), bananas, oil palm, rubber and tea.
- **Food crops**: cassava, plantain, maize, yams, groundnuts, beans.
- **Livestock**: cattle in the Adamawa, North and North-West.
- **Fishing** on the coast, rivers and Lake Chad.
- **Timber** from the forests of the East and South.
- **Petroleum** from the sea near the coast; **tourism** and **trade**.

blocks.title: Transport
blocks.md: Cameroon uses **roads** (the most used), **railways** (Douala-Yaoundé and Yaoundé-Ngaoundéré), **rivers and the sea** (the ports of **Douala** and **Kribi**), and **air** (international airports at Douala and Yaoundé, and others). Good transport helps farmers to sell their crops and brings goods to the towns. Neighbouring countries such as Chad and the Central African Republic also use Cameroon's roads, railway and port.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Placing cocoa in the dry north or cotton in the rainforest.
- Calling a factory a primary activity: it is **secondary**.
- Thinking that only farming is work: teaching, driving and trading are also important activities.
- Forgetting that food processing (making oil from palm nuts) adds value to crops.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Classify as primary, secondary or tertiary: (a) growing cocoa, (b) making chocolate in a factory, (c) selling chocolate in a shop.
steps: (a) Growing cocoa takes a product from the land: primary.
(b) Making chocolate changes cocoa into a new product: secondary.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Why are roads important for farmers in the West Region?
steps: Farmers need to carry maize, vegetables and coffee to markets in towns.
Good roads make the journey faster and the goods stay fresh.
blocks.answer: They carry crops to markets quickly and cheaply, so farmers earn more.
